title: Grade 2 Math — Fri, May 29
description: 2D Shapes — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — shapes, sides, corners, real life
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Riya sees 2 triangles and 3 squares. How many corners does she see in total?
questions.explanation: 2 triangles × 3 corners = 6 corners. 3 squares × 4 corners = 12 corners. 6 + 12 = 18.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE?
options: A square is NOT a rectangle
A rectangle is always a square
A square is a special rectangle with all equal sides
questions.explanation: A square IS a rectangle — it has 4 sides and 4 right angles. But it is special because all 4 sides are equal.

questions.question: A school has 4 triangular windows and 6 rectangular windows. How many corners are there in total?
Sort these by number of sides (least to most): Hexagon, Triangle, Square, Pentagon.
questions.explanation: Triangle (3) < Square (4) < Pentagon (5) < Hexagon (6). Sorted from least to most sides.

questions.question: What is the total number of sides in: 1 triangle + 1 rectangle + 1 pentagon?
Arjun draws 5 shapes each with 6 sides. What shape did he draw, and how many sides in total?
questions.explanation: 6-sided shape = hexagon. 5 hexagons × 6 sides = 30 sides total.

questions.question: Which shape can tile a floor WITHOUT leaving gaps: circle or square?
questions.explanation: Squares tile perfectly — no gaps. Circles leave gaps between them because they are round.

questions.question: A shape has 8 sides. What is it called, and how many corners does it have?
questions.explanation: 8 sides = octagon. An octagon has 8 corners (same as sides).

questions.question: Which 2D shape has no straight edges and no corners?
questions.explanation: A circle is the only common 2D shape with no straight edges and no corners — it is perfectly curved.

questions.question: Priya has 3 squares and cuts each one diagonally into 2 triangles. How many triangles does she have?
questions.explanation: Each square cut diagonally = 2 triangles. 3 squares × 2 = 6 triangles.

questions.question: Name a shape that has both equal sides AND equal corners:
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 equal corners (all 90 degrees). A rectangle has equal corners but unequal sides.

questions.question: A classroom has 3 hexagonal mats and 2 triangular mats. How many total sides?
questions.explanation: 3 hexagons × 6 sides = 18 sides. 2 triangles × 3 sides = 6 sides. 18 + 6 = 24.

questions.question: All rectangles have ___ right-angle corners.
questions.explanation: All rectangles (and squares) have exactly 4 right-angle (90-degree) corners — that is what makes them rectangles.

questions.question: A shape with 5 corners is always called a ___.
questions.explanation: 5 corners = 5 sides = pentagon. The number of sides and corners are always equal in any polygon.

questions.question: Week summary: which is the BEST sentence about 2D shapes?
options: All 2D shapes have the same number of sides
Squares and rectangles both have 4 sides, but only squares have all equal sides
questions.explanation: The key insight this week: Squares and rectangles both have 4 sides, but a square's 4 sides are all equal length — making it a special rectangle.
